lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works remotely with Wichita businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. Wichita calls itself the Air Capital of the World, and aircraft manufacturing still shapes the city, alongside healthcare, energy and agriculture. We help Wichita companies reach the buyers they need, from aerospace procurement teams to families on the east and west sides of town.

sections.heading: A city that builds aircraft
paragraphs: Wichita has made aeroplanes since the early days of flight. Cessna and Beechcraft both began here and are still built in the city, business jets are serviced and completed here, and a very large plant produces fuselages and other major structures for airliners. McConnell Air Force Base sits on the southeast side, and Wichita State University runs a well-known aviation research institute.

Around the big names is a supply chain of machine shops, composite specialists, tooling firms, finishers and engineering contractors. They sell to quality-minded buyers who look for approvals, equipment lists and evidence of similar work. A supplier's website is often checked before a request for quote is sent, so it has to answer those questions directly.
bullets: Capability pages listing processes, machines, materials and approvals.
Search visibility for the exact services procurement teams look for.
LinkedIn campaigns aimed at buyers and engineers in chosen industries.
Hiring pages that help recruit skilled machinists and technicians.

sections.heading: East side, west side and the towns around
paragraphs: Kellogg Avenue runs east to west through the city and most people describe where they live by which side they are on. The east side, toward Andover, and the west side, toward Goddard and Maize, each have their own shopping areas, medical offices and restaurants, and residents tend to stay on their side for everyday needs. Derby and Haysville lie to the south.

Closer in, Old Town's brick warehouses hold restaurants, bars and offices. Delano, just across the Arkansas River, and the Douglas Design District have independent shops, and College Hill and Riverside are established residential neighbourhoods. Wichita is also the regional centre for a large part of Kansas, so its hospitals, dealers and specialists draw people from many counties away.

sections.heading: Local search and the Wichita calendar
paragraphs: For a business serving households, map results matter most. That means a complete business profile, pages that mention the side of town and the suburbs you cover, and a steady supply of honest reviews. Wichita customers value local ownership, and saying plainly that you are a Wichita company helps.

Spring is storm season on the plains. Hail can damage thousands of roofs and cars in one afternoon, and searches surge straight away. Local roofers and repair shops should have pages and ads ready in advance. Riverfest brings crowds downtown as summer begins, and hot summers and cold winters keep heating and cooling firms busy at both ends of the year.

faqs.a: No. We work with Wichita businesses remotely, with video meetings and regular reports.

faqs.q: Can marketing help an aerospace supplier find work outside aviation?
faqs.a: Yes. We create pages that present your capabilities for another industry, such as defence or medical devices, make them visible in search, and run campaigns aimed at buyers in that field. Results take time because approval and qualification processes are slow.

faqs.q: How do I get more calls after a hail storm in Wichita?
faqs.a: Prepare before the season. Have a storm damage page live, ad campaigns built and paused, and your business profile up to date with recent reviews. When a storm hits, switch the ads on for the affected areas the same day.

faqs.q: How much does digital marketing cost in Wichita?
faqs.a: It depends on the scope of work and the channels you need. We provide a quote following a free consultation.

faqs.q: Do I need separate pages for east and west Wichita?
faqs.a: If you serve both and have something specific to say about each, yes. It helps you appear for searches that name an area. A business with one location should still mention the parts of town and suburbs it covers.
